first.title: A project that runs, from a template
first.then: THE PROJECT IS UP - the result above says what AMAL made it from and holds its map (PROJECT_MAP: its scenes, scripts and input actions). A WORKING TEMPLATE (any start but an empty project) IS ALREADY A GAME THAT PLAYS - do not read through its files and do not plan it again: (a) `godot_check` it once; (b) when his words ask for something it does not already have, do only that, one small change at a time, each checked with godot_check, reading only the file a change touches; a premade character in place of the game's own is two calls - `premade` (search by his words, then get) and `godot_swap` with the file it fetched - never hand edits to scene files; AMAL itself proves each change when you `finish`: it plays the game through every one of its input actions, sets the pictures beside the ones from before the change, and sends you back if what he asked does not show - so do not `godot_play` or `look` to prove a change yourself, just make it, godot_check it and finish; (c) when his words ask nothing beyond what it already is ("make a platformer" and it is a platformer), `finish` now and tell him in three lines what the game is, how it is played (the map's input actions) and what he can ask for next - its look, premade characters in place of its own, another level, a rule. AN EMPTY PROJECT: build, working copy first: (1) a BLOCKOUT of what he asked - the smallest version that plays, with grey boxes, plain shapes and placeholder text for everything (no art, no add-ons, no research beyond what this step needs) - then godot_check and godot_play it and show him the running game with tell_owner; (2) only then add detail, one small playable step at a time, each checked the same way. Plan at most five tasks, the first of them the blockout that plays. Never write project.godot or a .tscn scene by hand as text (their resource lines break and Godot cannot read them): build the blockout's nodes in GDScript - created in the main scene's script when it starts (CharacterBody3D.new(), MeshInstance3D with a CapsuleMesh or BoxMesh, CollisionShape3D, Camera3D, add_child) - or, for a scene to keep, a builder script run once with `godot --headless --path "<project>" --script res://tools/build_<scene>.gd` that makes the nodes, sets each one's owner, and saves with PackedScene.pack() and ResourceSaver.save(). Paths always in quotes. Characters and props come the way THE LINE'S SETTINGS (Characters) and ASSETS say: asked once, premade put in as soon as the blockout plays - they are already rigged and animated, so the work is the look (materials, lights, scale, the right clip on the right action), not rigging. Add nothing he did not ask for.
